paragraphs: The first public libraries in Australia opened in the nineteenth century.
They were often funded by local councils together with wealthy donors.
These donors hoped that free access to books would improve working people's education.
Today, the same idea continues through free digital loans and online resources.
Many students find it difficult to manage their time at university.
Unlike at school, they are rarely told exactly when to study.
As a result, assignments are often left until the last minute.
To avoid this, study skills advisers recommend creating a weekly timetable.
Such a plan makes large tasks feel more manageable.
The kea is a large parrot found in the mountains of New Zealand's South Island.
It is famous for its intelligence and curiosity.
For example, kea have been observed solving puzzles and using simple tools in experiments.
However, this curiosity sometimes leads them to damage cars and equipment left by visitors.
Economists have long debated why some countries grow richer than others.
One early explanation focused on natural resources such as land and minerals.
Yet several resource-poor countries have achieved rapid economic growth.
This has led researchers to emphasise institutions, education and trade instead.
These factors appear to shape how effectively a country uses its resources.
Recycling programmes depend on people sorting their waste correctly.
When non-recyclable items are placed in recycling bins, the whole load can be contaminated.
Contaminated loads are often sent to landfill instead of being processed.
For this reason, many councils now run education campaigns explaining what can be recycled.
In the past, maps were drawn by hand using measurements taken on the ground.
This process was slow and could take many years for a single region.
The introduction of aerial photography in the twentieth century made mapping much faster.
More recently, satellites have allowed the entire planet to be mapped in great detail.
A placebo is a treatment that contains no active ingredient.
Despite this, patients who receive one often report feeling better.
Researchers believe this effect is linked to patients' expectations.
Because of this, new medicines are always tested against a placebo in clinical trials.
Only drugs that perform better than the placebo are considered effective.
Coral reefs cover a tiny fraction of the ocean floor.
Nevertheless, they support around a quarter of all known marine species.
This makes them one of the most biologically diverse ecosystems on Earth.
Unfortunately, rising sea temperatures are putting many reefs at serious risk.
When applying for a job, a well-written cover letter can make a strong first impression.
It should begin by stating clearly which position the applicant is interested in.
The following paragraphs should explain how the applicant's skills match the role.
Finally, the letter should thank the employer and express interest in an interview.
The printing press was developed in Europe in the fifteenth century.
Before its invention, books had to be copied by hand.
This meant they were extremely expensive and available only to a small elite.
Printing dramatically reduced the cost of producing books.
Consequently, ideas could spread much more quickly across the continent.
Bees play a vital role in food production.
As they collect nectar, they carry pollen from one flower to another.
This process allows many crops to produce fruit and seeds.
Without bees, the yields of foods such as apples and almonds would fall sharply.
Sleep plays an important role in learning.
During sleep, the brain processes information gathered during the day.
Studies show that students who sleep well after studying remember more the next day.
It is therefore unwise to stay awake all night before an exam.
Urban planners increasingly talk about the fifteen-minute city.
The idea is that residents should be able to reach most daily needs within a short walk or bike ride.
These needs include schools, shops, health services and parks.
Supporters argue that such neighbourhoods reduce car use and strengthen communities.
Critics, however, worry that the concept may be difficult to apply in existing suburbs.
Tea originated in China thousands of years ago.
From there, it spread to Japan and other parts of Asia.
In the seventeenth century, European traders began importing it.
It soon became a popular drink in Britain, where it remains a cultural tradition.
Volunteering can benefit both communities and volunteers themselves.
Community groups gain extra help without having to pay wages.
Meanwhile, volunteers develop new skills and social connections.
Some studies even suggest that regular volunteering improves mental wellbeing.
Scientists first noticed the hole in the ozone layer over Antarctica in the nineteen eighties.
They traced it to chemicals called CFCs, which were used in refrigerators and spray cans.
In response, countries signed an international agreement to phase out these chemicals.
Since then, the ozone layer has slowly begun to recover.
The agreement is often cited as an example of successful global cooperation.
Online shopping has grown rapidly over the past two decades.
One reason is convenience, since consumers can compare prices and order from home.
However, this growth has created challenges for traditional shops.
Many have responded by offering click-and-collect services and improving their own websites.
The Southern Alps run along the length of New Zealand's South Island.
They were formed where the Pacific and Australian plates collide.
This collision continues to push the mountains upwards each year.
At the same time, heavy rainfall and glaciers wear them away.
Researchers have long studied how people make decisions about money.
Traditional theories assumed that people always act rationally.
In practice, however, choices are often influenced by emotions and habits.
This observation gave rise to the field of behavioural economics.
Its findings are now used to design policies such as automatic enrolment in savings schemes.
Writing a literature review is a key step in any research project.
First, the researcher searches for relevant books and articles.
Next, these sources are read carefully and compared.
The review then summarises what is already known and identifies gaps in the research.
Electric scooters have appeared in many cities in recent years.
Users can hire them through an app and leave them almost anywhere.
This flexibility has made them popular for short trips.
However, scooters left on footpaths have caused complaints from pedestrians.
Glaciers are often described as rivers of ice.
They form when snow accumulates over many years and is compressed into ice.
Under its own weight, this ice slowly flows downhill.
As glaciers move, they carve valleys and transport large amounts of rock.
Many of the world's most dramatic landscapes were shaped in this way.
The Olympic Games were first held in ancient Greece.
They were part of a religious festival honouring the god Zeus.
After being banned for centuries, the Games were revived in eighteen ninety-six.
Today, they have grown into one of the largest international events in the world.
Many people struggle to drink enough water during the day.
Mild dehydration can cause headaches and reduce concentration.
One simple solution is to carry a reusable water bottle.
Having water within easy reach makes it more likely that people will drink regularly.
Wetlands were once widely regarded as useless land.
As a result, large areas were drained for farming and development.
Scientists now understand that wetlands filter water and reduce flooding.
This has led to growing efforts to protect and restore them.
Some farmers are even creating small wetlands on their own land.
Job interviews can be stressful for many applicants.
Preparation is one of the most effective ways to reduce this stress.
This includes researching the organisation and practising answers to common questions.
Applicants who prepare well usually feel more confident on the day.
Cane toads were introduced to Australia in the nineteen thirties.
They were brought in to control beetles that damaged sugar cane crops.
Unfortunately, the toads failed to control the beetles.
Instead, they spread rapidly and harmed native animals that tried to eat them.
Language changes constantly over time.
New words are created to describe new technologies and ideas.
At the same time, other words gradually fall out of use.
Grammar and pronunciation also shift, although more slowly.
This is why texts written several centuries ago can be difficult to understand today.
Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity.
Their price has fallen dramatically over the past decade.
Because of this, many households now install panels on their roofs.
Some also add batteries so they can use stored solar power at night.
Museums face the challenge of attracting younger visitors.
Traditional displays of objects behind glass may not appeal to them.
To address this, many museums have introduced interactive exhibits.
These allow visitors to touch, play and learn actively.
The first vaccine was developed in the late eighteenth century.
It protected people against smallpox, a deadly disease at the time.
Over the following centuries, vaccines were created for many other illnesses.
Eventually, a global vaccination campaign eliminated smallpox completely.
Many cities are planting more trees along their streets.
Trees provide shade, which helps to cool neighbourhoods in summer.
They also absorb rainwater and reduce the risk of flooding.
For these reasons, urban trees are increasingly seen as essential infrastructure.
Critical thinking is often listed as a key graduate attribute.
Yet students are not always sure what the term means.
In simple terms, it involves evaluating evidence before accepting a claim.
It also requires considering other points of view and possible weaknesses in an argument.
Developing this skill takes practice across many subjects.
The bicycle has a long and surprising history.
Early versions had no pedals and were pushed along with the feet.
Later, models with huge front wheels became popular but were dangerous.
The safer design used today appeared in the eighteen eighties.
Presentations are a common form of university assessment.
To prepare, students should first identify their main message.
They should then organise supporting points in a logical order.
Finally, rehearsing aloud helps them speak confidently and stay within the time limit.
Tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon.
As the Earth rotates, different areas pass through bulges of water created by this pull.
Because the Moon's movements are regular, tides can be predicted years in advance.
This predictability makes tidal energy an attractive source of renewable power.
However, only a few locations have tides strong enough to be used.
Food waste is a major problem in wealthy countries.
Much of it happens in homes rather than on farms.
People often buy more than they need or misunderstand date labels.
Planning meals and checking the fridge before shopping can reduce this waste.
The kiwi is New Zealand's national bird.
It cannot fly and is mostly active at night.
Because it nests on the ground, it is vulnerable to introduced predators such as stoats.
Conservation programmes now protect eggs and raise chicks in safe areas.
Social media platforms collect large amounts of data about their users.
This information is used to show people content they are likely to engage with.
Critics argue that this can trap users in bubbles of similar opinions.
Some researchers, however, suggest that the effect is smaller than often claimed.
The debate highlights how difficult it is to measure social media's influence.
Desalination turns seawater into fresh drinking water.
Most plants do this by pushing water through special membranes that remove salt.
The process uses a lot of energy, which makes it expensive.
Nevertheless, it provides a reliable supply for dry cities such as Perth.
Group study sessions can be very effective before exams.
Students can explain difficult concepts to each other.
Teaching others in this way often strengthens their own understanding.
However, sessions work best when the group agrees on clear goals beforehand.
Historians rely on many different kinds of sources.
Written documents, such as letters and official records, are the most familiar.
However, these often reflect the views of people with power and education.
For this reason, historians also study oral histories, objects and archaeological remains.
Together, these sources give a more complete picture of the past.
Earthquakes cannot be predicted precisely.
However, scientists can identify regions where they are likely to occur.
In these areas, strict building codes help structures withstand shaking.
Public education also teaches people what to do when an earthquake strikes.
Coffee is one of the world's most widely traded products.
Most of it is grown by small farmers in tropical countries.
These farmers often receive only a small share of the final price.
Fair trade schemes aim to give them a more stable and reasonable income.
Antibiotic resistance is a growing threat to global health.
It develops when bacteria survive treatment and pass on their resistance.
The overuse of antibiotics speeds up this process considerably.
To slow it down, doctors are encouraged to prescribe antibiotics only when necessary.
Researchers are also searching for entirely new types of treatment.
